title: P75 (Papyrus Hanna 1): John 2:12-3:3 (fol. 46r)
source: Papyrus Hanna 1 (Mater Verbi), Vatican Library: photographs from DigiVatLib; Greek from the INTF NTVMR transcription of P75; English from the King James Version
description: John 2:12-3:3 in P75 (Papyrus Hanna 1), the papyrus codex of Luke and John copied around 175-225: fol. 46r, each page with its photograph, the Greek transcription and the King James Version.
introduction:
P75 is a papyrus codex of Luke and John copied in Egypt around 175-225, the oldest known copy of Luke and one of the oldest of John. It was bought by Martin Bodmer in the 1950s and published as Papyrus Bodmer XIV-XV; in 2006 it was given to the Vatican Library, where it is kept as Papyrus Hanna 1 (Mater Verbi). Its text is very close to that of Codex Vaticanus, written some 150 years later. Where Luke ends and John begins (folio 44r) both titles stand on the same page.

About 51 leaves survive, many damaged at the top and edges, especially in Luke 3-7. Lost: Luke 1:1-3:17, most of 3:23-4:33, 5:11-36, 6:5-10, 7:33-34 and 7:44-45 (and parts of 7:36-49), 17:16-19, 18:19-22:3; John 11:46-47, 12:1-2, 13:11-14:7 and everything after 15:10 except small fragments. Each section below is one page: the photograph, the NTVMR diplomatic transcription line by line, and the King James Version of every verse on the page. Where P75 lacks a verse or words that the KJV has (for example John 5:4 or the account of the adulteress, John 7:53-8:11), the section says so. Six damaged pages (folios 7v, 11r, 39v, 58r, 58v and 64v) are left out because their text could not be matched to the photographs with certainty.

This entry covers fol. 46r (John 2:12-3:3), shown on the Vatican Library's photograph (frame 2A.10r).
translator_notes: Greek: the NTVMR diplomatic transcription, line by line as on the papyrus. Square brackets enclose letters that are lost or illegible and were supplied by the transcribers; a dot under a letter marks it as uncertain; [...] marks a gap. Nomina sacra and numerals keep the scribe's overline. Spelling is the scribe's (no accents or breathings). Words broken at a line end stay broken as on the papyrus. Corrections are not shown: the text is the first hand.

English: the King James Version (1611), whole verses, for every verse that has text on the page. A verse that begins on one page and ends on the next is given in full on both. The KJV translates a later form of the Greek text, so its wording does not always match the papyrus; material differences (such as verses the papyrus does not have) are noted in the section.

translation.text: <sup>2:12</sup>¶ After this he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, and his brethren, and his disciples: and they continued there not many days. <sup>13</sup>¶ And the Jews’ passover was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem, <sup>14</sup>And found in the temple those that sold oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting: <sup>15</sup>And when he had made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers’ money, and overthrew the tables; <sup>16</sup>And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house an house of merchandise. <sup>17</sup>And his disciples remembered that it was written, The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up. <sup>18</sup>¶ Then answered the Jews and said unto him, What sign shewest thou unto us, seeing that thou doest these things? <sup>19</sup>Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. <sup>20</sup>Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days? <sup>21</sup>But he spake of the temple of his body. <sup>22</sup>When therefore he was risen from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this unto them; and they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said. <sup>23</sup>¶ Now when he was in Jerusalem at the passover, in the feast day, many believed in his name, when they saw the miracles which he did. <sup>24</sup>But Jesus did not commit himself unto them, because he knew all men, <sup>25</sup>And needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man. <sup>3:1</sup>There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews: <sup>2</sup>The same came to Jesus by night, and said unto him, Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God: for no man can do these miracles that thou doest, except God be with him. <sup>3</sup>Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he can not see the kingdom of God.

NTVMR page 670 (folio 46r). 2:12 begins on the previous page; 3:3 continues on the next page. Checked on the image: near the top περι του ναου του σωματος αυτου (2:21), last line ειπεν αυτω αμην αμην λεγω σοι (3:3), matching the transcription of this page.
